Record unavailable importer capabilities rather than pretending a suitable scripted component does not exist. Choose reasonable details yourself; no saving, multiplayer, purchases or large map. Success needs observed press/pop/recovery timing, per-bubble state, exact counting, sheet completion/reset and usable desktop/touch input. Do not claim success from code inspection alone.

spec.assetStrategy:
Begin with complete Marketplace Model discovery for an interactive bubble-wrap or bubble-pop system, not a static sheet. Inspect candidate hierarchy, source scripts, remotes, state model, animations, input handling, sounds, reset behavior, dependencies, and cleanup before assigning implementation ownership. Retain useful verified geometry, behavior, animation, and media, and adapt only the missing counter, validation, completion, reset, HUD, lifecycle, or device integration established by that inspection. Script paths for discovery-dependent glue intentionally remain unassigned until the selected component’s actual interfaces are known.

Embedded audio must retain Marketplace provenance and undergo loading, playback, synchronization, and listening checks. Only if inspection establishes that the complete component lacks usable audio should the separate Audio need be searched. Standalone animation retrieval is not assumed; animation should preferably come inside the complete Model. If a promising candidate contains scripts, rigs, packages, or serialization that the importer cannot preserve, record the exact capability gap and escalate it rather than treating the candidate as absent or silently rebuilding it. No asset IDs, compatibility claims, or successful media tests are assumed in this plan.
spec.title: Bubble Break ASMR Tabletop
spec.summary:
A compact one-player tabletop bubble-wrap experience for desktop and touch. The player spawns safely beside a small, warmly lit desk with the reusable bubble sheet filling the close gameplay view. Minimal guidance invites the player to click or tap any raised bubble. A valid press locks that bubble, visibly compresses it, plays a synchronized Marketplace pop, settles it into a popped state, and only then advances the counter by exactly one. The player continues until every bubble on the sheet is popped, receives clear completion feedback, and deliberately chooses Reset Sheet to restore a fresh layout and zero counter.

The planned sheet contains at least twelve individually addressable bubbles, preferably a readable 4-by-4 arrangement if the selected reusable Marketplace component supports it. The imported component’s geometry, scripts, animations, sounds, interfaces, and dependencies must be inspected before any replacement or glue implementation is assigned. The tabletop remains a small focused interaction area: safe spawn/stool position, central sheet, restrained desk dressing, close camera framing, and boundaries that prevent irrelevant travel. There is no saving, economy, purchase flow, progression system, combat, or large map.

Authoritative session state belongs to the server: sheet generation, each bubble’s ready/pressing/popped phase, rate checks, distance checks, exact counter increments, completion, and reset eligibility. The client is responsible for pointer/touch intent, close presentation, HUD, and local visual responsiveness only; it cannot award pops. Assumptions chosen as requested: a quiet warm desk setting, a preferred 16-bubble layout where compatible with the retained component, a short approximately 0.15–0.35 second press-to-settle sequence, and a persistent depressed appearance until reset. Final acceptance requires native gameplay observation and audible playback, not code inspection.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a close, tactile ASMR product-shot composition rather than a broad room. The central landmark is a translucent, slightly cool-tinted bubble sheet on a warm matte wood tabletop. A chair or safe standing position places the avatar within validated interaction distance, while the gameplay camera frames the whole sheet at a shallow overhead angle. Edge dressing may include a softly shaped desk mat, small lamp, and restrained background objects, but these remain noninteractive and must not compete with the bubbles.

Shape language should be soft and rounded: circular bubble domes, rounded sheet corners, beveled UI panels, and gentle pools of light. Ready bubbles must read as raised and glossy; a pressing bubble visibly compresses through a brief staged motion; a popped bubble remains flattened or inverted with reduced highlight so its state is unmistakable. Avoid excessive particles, screen shake, neon colors, or arcade clutter. The press animation and audio synchronization are the primary reward.

Use a warm neutral environment palette with the sheet as the cool focal accent. Maintain strong value contrast between tabletop, bubble edges, and pressed states. Lighting should make dome silhouettes and deformation readable without harsh reflections. Keep all interactive bubbles large enough for reliable touch selection and leave clear spacing between hit regions.

The HUD should be minimal: a compact high-contrast “Popped 0 / Total” counter and a clearly labeled Reset Sheet control. Reset remains deliberate and visually separated from bubble hit areas. At completion, show a restrained centered confirmation such as “Sheet Complete” with a gentle scale/fade treatment and make the reset action prominent. Desktop hover may provide a subtle highlight, while touch must not rely on hover. UI must respect safe areas and remain readable on common desktop and mobile aspect ratios.

spec.title: Sky Steps: Three-Checkpoint Cloud Run
spec.summary:
Create a compact single-player sky parkour course inside the supplied namespace. The route begins on a safe floating launch island around Y=100, advances through three checkpoints in strict order, crosses a moving platform over a visibly dangerous fall zone, and ends at a distinct finish platform. Comfortable jumps use broad landing surfaces and short, readable gaps rather than precision-heavy obstacles.

First-minute journey: from spawn, the player sees the first checkpoint ahead, cyan route markers, the moving-platform crossing in the middle distance, and the gold finish beacon beyond it. The first jumps teach ordinary traversal. Touching checkpoint 1 produces an obvious activation pulse and synchronized Marketplace confirmation sound. The player then rides the moving platform, continues through checkpoints 2 and 3, and reaches the finish. Falling into the marked hazard or below the course returns the character to the latest valid checkpoint while preserving progress and the active timer. Completion freezes the result and requires the player to deliberately choose Replay before a new run begins.

The server owns ordered progression, checkpoint positions, run timing, completion, replay validation, touch debounces, fall detection, and recovery. The client owns the readable HUD and replay input but cannot award progress or choose teleport destinations. Replicated server state provides an initial snapshot and observable changes so HUD state is not lost or missed during character respawns.

Marketplace checkpoint, moving-platform, and course systems must be discovered and inspected before integration. Their useful audited geometry, behavior, motion, animation, and media are retained. Missing rules are added as narrowly scoped glue after imported interfaces are known. Marketplace audio must load, play, and be heard during native checkpoint traversal. Unsupported scripts, dependencies, animation formats, or audio references are recorded as capability gaps rather than silently replaced. No persistence, purchases, combat, multiplayer competition, or sprawling secondary areas are included.
spec.visualDirection:
Use a bright, readable sky-island style with compact floating platforms, pale stone or white cloud-like structural surfaces, cyan route accents, warm gold finish accents, and high-contrast red/orange hazard markings. Platforms should use clean beveled or layered silhouettes rather than thin featureless slabs. Keep the route visible in sections from major landmarks so players can anticipate where to go next.

Compose the course along one gently turning forward route approximately 120–150 studs long and 35–50 studs wide. Spawn sits on a safe 16–22 stud landing island. Ordinary gaps should generally be about 5–8 studs with landing widths around 8–14 studs. The moving-platform crossing should be visually isolated over the hazard and have generous boarding and exit ledges. Checkpoints are unmistakable pads, rings, gates, or beacons placed directly on the traversal route. The finish uses a gold beacon or arch visible from earlier sections.

The hazard is not an ambiguous empty gap: use red/orange edge bands, warning chevrons, glow, particles, or another inspected component treatment around the fall area while retaining open sightlines to the sky below. Safe route surfaces remain cyan and white and must not visually resemble the hazard.

Checkpoint feedback visibly changes an accepted checkpoint through inspected existing animation or compatible pulse, light, color, or scale behavior added only if the retained component lacks it. The visual response and confirmation sound begin together when the server accepts the checkpoint. Later checkpoints touched out of order provide no activation or progress feedback.

The HUD is compact and high contrast. Current progress such as “Checkpoint 1 / 3” and an elapsed MM:SS.hh timer remain near the top edge without blocking traversal. Completion uses a centered result card with final time and a large Replay button. The button is comfortably tappable on touch and selectable on desktop. Layouts respect safe-area insets and remain legible at common phone and desktop resolutions.

First-minute journey: the player spawns on a safe platform facing a humanoid training dummy about 12 studs away. A clean floor lane and a six-stud range marker make the interaction distance readable. The HUD immediately shows the dummy at 100 health, zero accepted hits, a Light Attack control, and Reset. The player approaches, taps/clicks Light Attack, and sees an authorized windup, contact pose, impact reaction, health loss, counter increment, and synchronized impact sound. Continuing with correctly timed presses performs an escalating three-hit combo. Attacking from beyond range visibly misses, while holding or pressing during recovery produces no extra accepted strike. Two complete combos using 10/15/25 damage defeat the 100-health dummy. A short defeated state is followed by automatic restoration so practice can continue; the accepted-hit total remains visible until the player uses Reset, which restores health, clears the counter, and cancels the active sequence.

The authoritative combat sequence is server scheduled. For each discrete input edge, the server validates the player's living character, current arena state, combo timing, request rate, and recovery lock. At the scheduled contact instant it validates range again, applies damage at most once, increments the accepted-hit count only when damage is accepted, and replicates the resulting phase and feedback. The client owns device input and presentation but cannot claim damage, contact, combo index, range, or counter changes. State and subscriptions are cleaned on respawn, reset, defeat, and player departure. No PvP, matchmaking, saving, monetization, progression, or large-world systems are included.

spec.title: Strike Lab: 1-Player Training Arena
spec.summary: Strike Lab is a clean, responsive single-player fighting game training arena designed for desktop and touch. Upon spawning in a minimalist indoor dojo/lab ring, the player approaches an interactive humanoid training dummy. Pressing or tapping the strike input initiates a deterministic 3-hit light-attack sequence (Jab -> Cross -> Hook) with distinct windup, active contact, and recovery animation phases. The server strictly validates attack range (under 6.5 studs) and contact timing windows to prevent button-holding or recovery spam exploits. On verified hit, dummy health decreases, the active combo hit counter increments, distinct impact audio plays, and hit sparks appear. On miss or out-of-range swings, a light whoosh sound and miss indicator trigger with zero damage and no combo increment. When the dummy is defeated (0 HP), it ragdolls/dissolves and automatically resets after a short delay, with an explicit manual Reset Dummy button always available on the HUD. Touch controls provide dedicated on-screen strike and reset buttons alongside desktop keyboard/mouse input.
spec.visualDirection: A modern, high-contrast training dojo / martial arts laboratory. Clean floor grid with distinct ring boundaries marked by neon floor lines. A dedicated central training platform hosts the humanoid sparring dummy. Clean, readable HUD with crisp combo counter styling, dummy health bar with damage lag indicator, attack phase indicator (Windup/Active/Recovery), and mobile-friendly touch action buttons. Particle effects include sharp directional impact sparks for clean hits and subtle air streaks for misses.
